extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and agents (filing PCT national-phase applications in Singapore)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and formal requirements for entering the Singapore national phase from a PCT application, plus related filing, publication, amendment and search/examination rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT purpose and single international filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) facilitates seeking patent protection in several countries simultaneously by filing an international application with a single office, in one language and a single set of forms and fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a PCT request constitutes automatic designation of all Contracting States on the international filing date; on completion of the international phase the applicant must enter national phase into countries where protection is sought (e.g., by filing Patents Form 37 in Singapore).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of international phase and national phase timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The international phase runs from filing the international application until national phase begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normal national phase begins on expiry of 30 months from the earliest declared priority date (or filing date if no priority). Early national phase begins when Patents Form 37 is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents Form 37: required indications
rubrics_metrics.description: At national phase filing (Patents Form 37) applicants should indicate whether they seek early national phase entry and any changes in applicant(s)/inventor(s) names or addresses previously recorded with the PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If names/addresses changed during the international phase, furnish PCT/IB/306 to evidence the recordal before the PCT to facilitate processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation and format of Singapore application number for national phase entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submission of Patents Form 37, an application number will be allocated in the format TTYYYYXXXXC (with TT=type, 11=international application entering national phase in Singapore, YYYY=year, XXXXX=running numbers, C=check alphabet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different formats apply for applications lodged before 14 Feb 2014. If applicant is a Singapore corporate, UEN must be entered; otherwise the system will allocate an entity code.

rubrics_metrics.name: System retrieval of WIPO/PCT data on Form 37 filing
rubrics_metrics.description: On successful filing of Patents Form 37 the system will retrieve PCT data from WIPO for published PCT applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retrieved items include international filing date, publication number, applicant and inventor details, priority details, specification, reports (ISR, IPRP and annexed Article 34 amendments), Article 19 amendments, chapter I/II entry, publication language, and whether the PCT application was withdrawn. For non-published PCTs the system will retrieve data once published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of filing checks — core requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A date of filing will be accorded only if several formal requirements are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include: (a) fee paid; (b) Singapore address for service furnished; (c) applicant details in Form 37 auto-populate or match WIPO; (d) either early national phase requested or normal entry made between 29.5 to 30 months; (e) PCT published at WIPO in English (or other conditions below); (f) if PCT not published and early entry requested, enclose copy of PCT request form, specification and abstract and necessary English translation; (g) for non-English PCTs, enclose English translation and a Verification of English Translation (VET), where VET may be submitted within 2 months from national phase entry due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation rules and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: English translation of the specification must be submitted with Patents Form 37 unless an extension is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translation is submitted after national phase entry due date, request an extension on Patents Form 45 before the end of 18 months from expiry of the original timeline. Extensions beyond 18 months are possible if Registrar is satisfied the applicant has continuing intent to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required characteristics of translated documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Translations must meet formatting and reproduction standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings must be executed in black with sufficiently dense/dark strokes (no colour); documents must be legible and suitable for direct reproduction; documents must commence on a new sheet and sheets must be numbered consecutively, with drawings numbered as a separate series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of English Translation (VET) content
rubrics_metrics.description: VET must attest to accuracy and translator competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VET should state the document being translated; verify the translation corresponds to the original; state the translator's name and that they are well versed in English and the foreign language; include signature and date. Applicant may request extension of time to submit VET via Rule 108(1) eCommunications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of PCT-phase amendments (Article 19/34) at national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments made during the international phase in accordance with the PCT shall be treated as being made under the Singapore Patents Act if the copy of amendments has been communicated to the Registry (e.g., made available on PATENTSCOPE or submitted to the Registrar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an English translation of such amendments has not been filed within prescribed time limits, the amendment will be disregarded. An English translation of amendments and the VET should be submitted with Patents Form 37; if one of the necessary translations is missing, a notice will be issued to furnish the required translation within 2 months from notification. Multiple extension requests up to 18 months from the expiry of the original timeline may be made on Patents Form 45; extensions beyond 18 months require Registrar satisfaction of continuing intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold for early-filed Patents Form 37 before 29.5 months
rubrics_metrics.description: If Patents Form 37 is filed before 29.5 months and early national phase entry is not requested, the request will be put on hold until 29.5 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an automatic procedural hold; applicants should indicate early entry explicitly if they wish immediate processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities officer notification and rectify timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If formal requirements are not met, the Formalities officer will invite the applicant to clarify or rectify within 2 months from the date of the letter; a reminder will be issued if unresolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where requirements remain unmet by deadlines the application may be treated as withdrawn or the request refused depending on context; applicants may reply via eCommunications and use specified forms for corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms for corrections, amendments and types of changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific forms must be used for different corrections and recordals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change specification (description/claims/drawings/sequence listing): Patents Form 13 or Form CM4. To change abstract: Patents Form 13 or Form CM4. To rectify errors on Patents Form 37: Form CM4. To change name/address/agent details after international phase: Form CM2. To register transfer of ownership (assignment): Form CM8. For correction of error generally, refer to Chapter 11.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions causing application to be treated as withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: An application will be treated as withdrawn if certain conditions are unmet by the timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example conditions: failure to submit English translation of a PCT application published in a non-English language; failure to pay the prescribed fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time relating to Formalities Examination Adverse Report
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may request multiple extensions of time up to 18 months from the original timeline to respond to Formalities Examination Adverse Report; extensions beyond 18 months possible with Registrar's satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for extension should be made on Patents Form 45 before the end of 18 months from expiry of the original timeline. For extensions beyond 18 months, applicant must satisfy the Registrar of continuing underlying intention to proceed with the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of date of filing and completion of formalities check
rubrics_metrics.description: When all date-of-filing requirements are met, applicant will be issued a notification of date of filing; entry will be made in the register and the next Patents Journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once date-of-filing notification issued, formalities check for Patents Form 37 is complete and applicant may request search/examination reports (Patents Form 11, 12, 12A) if not already requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing applicability at national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapters 2.2.26 to 2.2.39 (sequence listing rules) are applicable with necessary modification to sequence listings filed at national phase entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants filing sequence listings at national phase should consult the referenced chapters for required modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordal of changes under Rule 92bis (use of PCT/IB/306)
rubrics_metrics.description: If changes are recordal-requested under Rule 92bis, the International Bureau will issue PCT/IB/306 and publish the changes in WIPO; changes made in the international phase should be submitted to the Registrar (e.g., via PCT/IB/306) to be taken into account in national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If changes were made in international phase and PCT/IB/306 furnished to Registrar via eCommunications, Formalities officer will update the national-phase record accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and outcomes for discrepancies in applicant name between PCT and Form 37
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant name differs between PCT Gazette and Patents Form 37 filing, the Registry will issue filing notifications and letters and may update records upon receiving PCT/IB/306 or appropriate forms (CM4/CM8/CM2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate outcomes: (1) PCT/IB/306 provided → notification issued in corrected name; (2) assignment during international phase not notified to PCT → provide Form CM8 to record assignment and publication in Patents Journal; (3) change of name not notified to PCT → provide Form CM2 to record change in national phase. Notification of date of filing may be issued in original PCT name with statements like 'Pending the recordal of the assignment/change'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and effects (18-month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications accorded a date of filing will be published in the Patents Journal as soon as possible after 18 months from the declared priority date (or filing date if no priority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications treated as withdrawn/abandoned/refused earlier than 1 month before the 18-month publication period will not be published. From publication until grant the applicant generally has same rights as if the patent had been granted on the publication date to bring proceedings for damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents Journal frequency and access to past issues
rubrics_metrics.description: From 26 May 2022, Patents Journals (A & B) publication frequency progressively increased to weekly (Patents Journal A: bibliographic actions; Journal B: abstract publication). Each issue available online at IPOS Digital Hub; past (non-online) issues can be requested (fee applies) and will be provided on CD-ROM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions on payment will be provided via email; acceptable payment modes include Internet Banking, Visa/Master cards, GIRO. Published patent application information is searchable via IPOS Digital Hub Search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for early publication (Patents Form 9) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant can request early publication by filing Patents Form 9 for strategic reasons, subject to formal checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities officer checks: (a) fee paid; (b) date of filing accorded; (c) national security clearance if applicable; (d) application not already published; (e) application not refused/abandoned/withdrawn (extensions possible if within allowable time); (f) no pending request for withdrawal (Form CM9); (g) representation/address for service on form corresponds with record (else file CM1/CM2). If requirements unmet applicant invited to rectify within 2 months; if met, request approved and entry made in register and Patents Journal; if objections cannot be overcome or no response, request refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of international application and translation (Section 86(7)/87)
rubrics_metrics.description: A PCT application entering national phase in Singapore is treated as published if it has been published in accordance with the PCT in English. For PCT applications published in a non-English language, no fee is required for publication of the translation for national phase entries on/after 26 May 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities officer will review that it is a PCT national phase entry, date of filing issued, PCT published at WIPO in non-English language, and that the translation filed is in order. When requirements met, register entry will be 'English translation of PCT application published in accordance to Section 86(7) of the Patents Act' at the Patents Journal publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments before grant — allowed subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may make voluntary amendments to the application or specification before grant provided the amendment does not disclose any additional matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary amendments should be requested using Patents Form 13 any time before grant except in specified situations (after certain search/exam requests or reports). Voluntary amendments can also be in Patents Form 13A in response to written opinions. Amendments in response to Registrar's formalities or to comply with formal requirements after Notice of Eligibility should also use Patents Form 13; amendments to specification after Notice of Intention to Refuse and when filing request for examination review report use Patents Form 12B procedures as relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and submission requirements for pre-grant amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: From 1 Apr 2017, both marked-up and clean copies of amended sheets are required for online submission; from 1 Dec 2019, if amendments or corrections have been made to claims, a marked-up and clean copy of the full set of claims must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments/corrections should be based on the latest set of specifications on record (including earlier same-day submissions or pending requests). The amendment request should set out reasons for amendments and any supporting evidence; it is highly encouraged to indicate the basis for amendments with references to particular parts of the application as filed. The Patent Examiner may request such basis during examination. Examples of accepted marked-up and clean copy formats are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: System checks for Patents Form 13 processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receiving Patents Form 13 the system will automatically review several requirements before processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks include: (a) application not granted (else use Patents Form 17); (b) application not refused/abandoned/withdrawn (extensions possible if within allowable time); (c) form filed within timelines; (d) representation/address for service correspond with record (else file CM1/CM2); (e) both marked-up and clean copies submitted. If requirements unmet, Formalities officer will send a letter to invite rectification within 2 months. If met, Formalities officer approves the request and enters event in register; amendments will be considered by the Patent Examiner during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple Patents Form 13 filings and withdrawal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If Patents Form 10, 11, 12 or 12A has not been filed, applicant can re-file a second Patents Form 13 for intended amendments (taking into account first PF13 approvals). Withdrawal of Patents Form 13 will not be permitted for approved cases; withdrawal may only be permitted for PF13 in processing or received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the search/exam forms have been filed, applicant should file Form CM4 and indicate the relevant rule for correction of error (Rules 58/91). See Chapter 11.8 for correction of error procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and examination route options
rubrics_metrics.description: After meeting formal requirements, applicant must choose a search/examination route.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: (a) Request for search report (Patents Form 10) followed by request for examination report (Patents Form 12); (b) Request for search and examination report (Patents Form 11); (c) Request for examination report (Patents Form 12) by relying on a local search report or final results of international search/examination or corresponding application; (d) Request for supplementary examination report (Patents Form 12A) by relying on final results of search/examination in international phase or related application. Annex provides definitions/examples of corresponding/related applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of search and examination processes and restriction practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Search involves a worldwide search for relevant materials; examination considers novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability and other requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application appears to relate to two or more inventions not part of a single inventive concept, examination may be restricted to the first invention specified in the claims and applicant will be notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limitations of supplementary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: For supplementary examination, the Patent Examiner will review specific grounds only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds include support, relatedness of claims, morality, methods of medical treatment or diagnosis, double patenting, and no added matter. From 30 Oct 2017, the Patent Examiner will also determine whether the invention defined in each claim constitutes patentable subject matter and, if not, will state full reasons in a written opinion. Note: applicants may no longer request supplementary examination reports for applications with date of filing on or after 1 Jan 2020 and divisional applications lodged on or after 1 Jan 2020.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on foreign search results/ISR when requesting examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant relies on foreign search results or the International Search Report (ISR), a copy of the search results should be submitted; if not in English, a translated copy is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All cited documents referred to in the search results must be submitted by the applicant. Translation of non-English cited documents is not required at the point of filing the request for examination, but the Patent Examiner may request translations where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for Registrar-supplied search/exam documents (post-26 May 2022)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Registrar has earlier sent a copy of the final results of the search or ISR in English to the applicant (e.g., where IPOS was the ISA), the applicant does not have to provide a copy of these documents when making a request for examination report on or after 26 May 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the applicant must still provide copies of Non-Patent Literature cited in the search results to the Registrar as these may not have been provided by the Registrar during the international phase (see Chapter 6.1.34).
